tagline: Trading wins, chemicals lose, and the strategy swings back to oil.

kpis.l: of Qatar LNG capacity knocked out for up to 5 years
buyback that wobbled on chemicals losses

lead_thesis: Shell earns from volatility it can't control while chemicals bleeds and the plan flips back to hydrocarbons.
lead_support: LNG is natural gas shipped cold by tanker. A buyback is the company buying its own shares. The fix: cost and margin visibility per plant, per cargo.

problems.heading: A war knocked out 17% of Qatar's LNG — Shell trades the swings
problems.fact: Q2 2026 profit more than doubled to $9.84B on trading and refining; Strait of Hormuz recovery is still uncertain.

calls.heading: Rank every cargo by margin-at-risk, daily
calls.sub: Know the best reroute before sailing.

calls.heading: Buy flexible landing slots, not fixed routes
calls.sub: Options beat schedules in a shock.

calls.heading: Take more LNG Canada volume while rivals pause
calls.sub: Cheap when the strait is shut.

calls.heading: Buy floating storage to bank the glut

problems.heading: Chemicals lost money — the $3.5B buyback wobbled
problems.fact: A February 2026 profit miss and a two-month buyback pause tied to a legal circular; trading profits masked the weak plants.

calls.heading: Show profit per plant, per product, monthly
Sell or close the two worst sites
Buybacks only after the cash lands
Turn the sites into power hubs
calls.sub: Use land and grid links for data or energy.

problems.heading: Shell doubled back to oil — $16.5B for ARC Resources

stat.cap: ARC deal incl. debt, closed Sept 2026

problems.fact: Meanwhile it sold Sprng Energy and its European renewables portfolio to TotalEnergies and took FID on LNG Canada Phase 2.

calls.heading: One page per asset: cash return and emissions
calls.sub: Same numbers for investors and regulators.

calls.heading: Stress every project at $60 oil
calls.sub: If it only works at $90, kill it.

calls.heading: Keep the best renewables, sell the rest
calls.sub: No trophy assets, no stranded costs.

calls.heading: Spin out the transition unit as its own company
calls.sub: Let the market fund the pivot.

booth.say: Shell makes money on volatility — so the edge is seeing price, cost and carbon sooner than the market.
ask: How do the trading desk and the plants share the same price view?
Which chemical sites still lack per-product margin visibility?
